name: employment-screening
description: The fairness-dimension taxonomy for automated resume screening and candidate ranking used in hiring.

dimensions.rationale: Under four-fifths rule analysis a selection rate gap is the primary statutory test, so the per-group pass rate must be published.
Features scraped from free-text resumes carry employer and school signals that act as proxies, so each feature needs a recorded justification.
Many jurisdictions prohibit using protected characteristics at all, not merely as a tiebreaker, so exclusion must be enforced at the serving boundary.
A feature is only defensible if it predicts performance in the target role, which requires a documented job-relatedness test.
Publishing rates for very small cohorts re-identifies applicants, so suppression and reporting thresholds must be stated.
Automated screening that reaches a rejection without review is the specific practice most jurisdictions now restrict.
An adverse decision a candidate cannot contest is not meaningfully human-reviewed, so the appeal route is part of the claim.
Applicant consent for automated evaluation varies by jurisdiction and is tracked but does not block attestation on its own.
